pr_title: JIT: inline shared generics with runtime lookups inside
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/81432
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/8662
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65815
_(probably more issues, need to check)_

Based on https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/81635.

This PR implements @jkotas's [idea](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/81432#issuecomment-1411268454) to inline shared generics which require runtime lookups.
Example:

```cs
[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
bool Test<T>() => Callee<T>();

bool Callee<T>() => typeof(T).IsValueType;
```
Codegen for `Test<string>` in Main:
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Program:Test[System.__Canon]():bool:this
       push     rbx
       sub      rsp, 48
       mov      qword ptr [rsp+0x28], rdx
       mov      rbx, rcx
       mov      rcx, qword ptr [rdx+0x10]
       mov      rax, qword ptr [rcx+0x10]
       test     rax, rax
       je       SHORT G_M000_IG04
       mov      rdx, rax
       jmp      SHORT G_M000_IG05
G_M000_IG04:
       mov      rcx, rdx
       mov      rdx, 0x7FFCC5FE7088
       call     CORINFO_HELP_RUNTIMEHANDLE_METHOD
       mov      rdx, rax
G_M000_IG05:
       mov      rcx, rbx
       call     [Program:Callee[System.__Canon]():bool:this]   ;;;  <---- not inlined
       nop      
       add      rsp, 48
       pop      rbx
       ret      
; Total bytes of code 68
```
Codegen for `Test<string>` in this PR:
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Program:Test[System.__Canon]():ubyte:this
       xor      eax, eax
       ret
```

I think the JIT side is ok (I just need to double check various "this context load is invariant" places), but I am not sure I implemented the VM side (only CoreCLR for now) correctly.

@MihuBot

@jkotas one thing I struggle with currently is when I have `tokenContext` being class (CORINFO_CONTEXTFLAGS_CLASS) -- how do I know whether to use `CORINFO_LOOKUP_CLASSPARAM` or `CORINFO_LOOKUP_THISOBJ` ?

> when I have tokenContext being class (CORINFO_CONTEXTFLAGS_CLASS) -- how do I know whether to use CORINFO_LOOKUP_CLASSPARAM or CORINFO_LOOKUP_THISOBJ

It is not possible to tell from `CORINFO_CONTEXTFLAGS_CLASS` context alone. You need to have the current method to figure it out.

> > when I have tokenContext being class (CORINFO_CONTEXTFLAGS_CLASS) -- how do I know whether to use CORINFO_LOOKUP_CLASSPARAM or CORINFO_LOOKUP_THISOBJ
> 
> It is not possible to tell from `CORINFO_CONTEXTFLAGS_CLASS` context alone. You need to have the current method to figure it out.

Current method as in the one we currently inline, right? not the `m_methodBeingCompiled` (which is the root method). So I presume I need to extend the JIT-EE interface
Although, I am not sure I understand where should I pass it, ComputeRuntimeLookupForSharedGenericToken is not a direct jit-ee api..

Right, the problem is that `CORINFO_RESOLVED_TOKEN::tokenContext` does not carry information about the method. For non-generic methods in generic types, we use the generic type as the context. We are doing that because we do not always have a `MethodDesc*` that represents the method on the generic type to use as the context. It may be possible to make these method desc, but it would be wasteful.

`CORINFO_CONTEXT_HANDLE` represents method or type today. I think you need to make `CORINFO_CONTEXT_HANDLE` to represent a method and type tuple, at least on the paths that lead to `ComputeRuntimeLookupForSharedGenericToken`. `ComputeRuntimeLookupForSharedGenericToken` would then use the method to tell the runtimeLookupKind to use [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6ebc8bd86dbc780b2a2a7daf3ab6020f9104f09e/src/coreclr/vm/jitinterface.cpp#L3096).

Changing `CORINFO_CONTEXT_HANDLE` into a struct that has two fields is probably the most straightforward way to do this.

> Changing `CORINFO_CONTEXT_HANDLE` into a struct that has two fields is probably the most straightforward way to do this.

I presume this adds 8 byte to a popular type that is used everywhere, I decided to propagate the containing Mth separately - it turned out to be easy, we need to compute the lookup from 3 places:
1) `getCallInfo` - it already had a "caller handle" parameter that represents exactly what I need - no change here
2) `embedGenericHandle` - I added "containingFtn" param here
3) `expandRawHandleIntrinsic` (NAOT-only API) - I added "containingFtn" param here as well

Now it seems to be passing CI and inlines way more shared generics (basically, all of them, we no longer give up on lookups)

An example (as I recall @stephentoub hit it somewhere relatively recently):
```cs
[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
int Foo<T>(Span<T> span) => Bar((ReadOnlySpan<T>)span); // forward to ROS<T> impl

int Bar<T>(ReadOnlySpan<T> span) => span.Length;
```
Codegen for `Foo<string>` in Main:
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Tests:Foo[System.__Canon](System.Span`1[System.__Canon])
       push     rbx
       sub      rsp, 64
       xor      eax, eax
       mov      qword ptr [rsp+0x28], rax
       mov      qword ptr [rsp+0x38], rdx
       mov      rbx, r8
       mov      rcx, qword ptr [rdx+0x38]
       mov      rax, qword ptr [rcx+0x10]
       test     rax, rax
       je       SHORT G_M21633_IG04
       mov      rdx, rax
       jmp      SHORT G_M21633_IG05
G_M21633_IG04:
       mov      rcx, rdx
       mov      rdx, 0x7FFC3F2C3498
       call     CORINFO_HELP_RUNTIMEHANDLE_METHOD
       mov      rdx, rax
G_M21633_IG05:
       lea      rcx, [rsp+0x28]
       mov      r8, rbx
       ;;;; NOT INLINED (requires runtime lookup)
       call     [System.Span`1[System.__Canon]:op_Implicit(System.Span`1[System.__Canon]):System.ReadOnlySpan`1[System.__Canon]]
       mov      eax, dword ptr [rsp+0x30]
       add      rsp, 64
       pop      rbx
       ret      
; Total bytes of code 83
```
New codegen `Foo<string>`:
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Tests:Foo[System.__Canon](System.Span`1[System.__Canon])
       mov      eax, dword ptr [r8+0x08]
       ret      
```

I managed to reduce repro to just `System.Buffers.SharedArrayPool'1<__Canon>.Rent(Int32)` method - it calls ComputeLookup 3 times (from jit's importer), seems to be for `{[S.P.CoreLib]System.GC.AllocateUninitializedArray<T>(int32,bool)}` call inside the `Rent` method.

> @jkotas @MichalStrehovsky I think I might need your help with NativeAOT (CoreCLR seems to be fine as is) 😞

I'll have a look at this in a couple hours but the immediate problem is that we're creating a non-sensical lookup (trying to do a generic lookup with System.Array as the context, that is clearly non-generic).

I submitted https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/99513 that adds an assert that is kicking in while there's still JIT code on the stack for this situation. That might be enough to help you here, but I can have another look.

I think the issue on native AOT is the same issue that was discussed above (and needs the same fix).

We call `embedGenericHandle`. This computes a lookup within the newly introduced `callerHandle`. In this case, `callerHandle` is a method on a generic type. This makes us note this is `CORINFO_LOOKUP_THISOBJ`.

The JIT then takes that information and feeds it to `getReadyToRunHelper`. But that one didn't get the `callerHandle` treatment so we fall back to `MethodBeingCompiled` as the context once it calls `GetGenericLookupHelper` (and also use the previously computed `CORINFO_LOOKUP_THISOBJ`), but that's wrong and ends up asserting (in the new assert I'm adding) because in this case `MethodBeingCompiled` is a generic method on a non-generic type.

We should be having the same problem for crossgen2 but maybe we just don't have enough testing?

I don't know how to fix that. It looks like this is going to require placing generic dictionary entries that are associated with X into generic dictionary Y. I guess this works with CoreCLR because it can add things to the generic dictionary any time it wants? I don't know how this gets reconciled. In .NET Native this worked because code generator kept track of things like "`__Canon`, but represents the T from `Rent`". We now have the Rent method and some other substitution from an inlined method and it's not clear to me how to build relationships between these (not to mention this looks like it will require the scanner predicting the inlining or we won't have a slot to hand out).
@jkotas should we for now enable it only for CoreCLR? I presume it will allow us to estimate beneifts (e.g. on dotnet/performance issue triaging) to see if it's worth the effort on NAOT side

> > I don't know how to fix that. It looks like this is going to require placing generic dictionary entries that are associated with X into generic dictionary Y.
> 
> This change should not be introducing any new dictionary slots. The dictionary lookups should be chained. The dictionary lookups in the inlinees should go through two or more existing slots.
> 
> @MichalStrehovsky Am I missing something?

Didn't realize it's chained. If it's chained, it might be fixable. I tried the straightforward fix (add the below into the `if (runtimeDep != null)` of `ShadowConcreteMethod.cs`:

```csharp
                        if (runtimeDep is ReadyToRunGenericLookupFromDictionaryNode lookupFromMethod
                            && (!canonMethod.RequiresInstMethodDescArg() || lookupFromMethod.DictionaryOwner != canonMethod))
                            continue;

                        if (runtimeDep is ReadyToRunGenericLookupFromTypeNode lookupFromType
                            && (!canonMethod.RequiresInstMethodTableArg() || (TypeDesc)lookupFromType.DictionaryOwner != canonMethod.OwningType))
                            continue;
```

It compiles, but we fail at object writing. I suspect this is because there's nothing that would report the dictionary dependencies for the inlined methods if there was no standalone method body generated for it anywhere. We cannot just skip it here, but also we don't have information to map this back to something that can be substituted.

I suspect this is only a problem if we're using the ReadyToRunGenericLookup helpers _and_ we're optimizing. This can only happen if `--noscan -O` was passed to ILC, or multimodule build.

A quick check would be to just drop the `/p:BuildFramework..` from here:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1400c1e7a888ea1e710e5c08d55c800e0b04bf8a/eng/pipelines/runtime.yml#L301

If it's only a problem for that, maybe we can somehow disable this inlining if ReadyToRun helpers are used and we're optimizing. I don't want to lose the ability to `--noscan -O` because it's sometimes useful for troubleshooting

issue_context.title: JIT: Don't give up on runtime lookup in inliner too early
issue_context.body:
```csharp
static bool Test<T>() => Callee<T>();

static bool Callee<T>() => typeof(T) == typeof(int);
```
It is expected that `Test<string>` will be compiled to just `return false`. Instead, it's compiled down to:
```asm
; Assembly listing for method Program:<<Main>$>g__Test|0_0[System.__Canon]():bool
G_M24604_IG01:
       sub      rsp, 40
       mov      qword ptr [rsp+20H], rcx
G_M24604_IG02:
       mov      rdx, qword ptr [rcx+38H]
       mov      rdx, qword ptr [rdx+10H]
       test     rdx, rdx
       je       SHORT G_M24604_IG04
G_M24604_IG03:
       jmp      SHORT G_M24604_IG05
G_M24604_IG04:
       mov      rdx, 0xD1FFAB1E      ; global ptr
       call     CORINFO_HELP_RUNTIMEHANDLE_METHOD
       mov      rdx, rax
G_M24604_IG05:
       mov      rcx, rdx
       call     [Program:<<Main>$>g__Callee|0_1[System.__Canon]():bool]
       nop      
G_M24604_IG06:
       add      rsp, 40
       ret      
; Total bytes of code 57
```
It seems that JIT's inliner could be a bit smarter here when currently it gives up when it sees `ldtoken T!` as a potential runtime lookup.  We either can teach it to recognize `typeof() == typeof()` idiom upfront (and fold) or we can do a sort of "I've just hit a runtime lookup, let me import up to 3 more opcodes to see if I will be able to fold it"
cc @AndyAyersMS @jkotas

Seems like it could be a bit clunky to engineer this?

A more natural thing might be to keep going until the next stack empty point or block boundary.

> A more natural thing might be to keep going until the next stack empty point

Even more natural thing to do would be to fix the problem with inlining dictionary lookups. Even imperfect (not 100% efficient) solution may be better than what we have today.

> > A more natural thing might be to keep going until the next stack empty point
> 
> Even more natural thing to do would be to fix the problem with inlining dictionary lookups. Even imperfect (not 100% efficient) solution may be better than what we have today.

Is it doable for e.g cross-assembly inlining?

cross-assembly inlining is not a problem

When one shared generic method calls another shared generic method, the flow is roughly:

1. Generic dictionary lookup of generic context in the caller
2. The generic context is passed as hidden argument
3. Generic dictionary lookup of the actual thing (e.g. type) in the callee

It should be doable to mimic this exact flow with inlining as a first iteration: 
- The inlined code would use chain of generic dictionary lookups to lookup the actual thing. It is not as efficient as it can be, but it is better than no inlining we get today. The VM should be able to fold the two generic lookups into a single generic lookup, but it requires inventing representation of new kind of types on the VM side that we were stuck on.
- The JIT should be able to dead-code eliminate the generic lookups if they end up unused (solves the problem described by this issue).

> It should be doable to mimic this exact flow with inlining as a first iteration:

Thanks, that sounds like a challenge/interesting task to do, will try this weekend, always wanted to know how this stuff works under the hood. My understanding that currently we give up somewhere [here in VM](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/842ec4aaa723daaf2ce5d6d8931d09773ae55831/src/coreclr/vm/jitinterface.cpp#L2828-L2831)

@jkotas @MichalStrehovsky is it easier to do for NativeAOT? It seems that the runtime lookup is much simpler there? e.g. for
```csharp
[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)]
static Type Test<T>() => Callee<T>();

static Type Callee<T>() => typeof(T);
```
Here is the codegen for both methods (`Test<string>` and `Callee<string>`):
```asm
; Method Prog:Test[System.__Canon]():System.Type
G_M18196_IG01:
       sub      rsp, 40
       mov      qword ptr [rsp+20H], rcx
G_M18196_IG02:
       mov      rcx, qword ptr [rcx]
       call     Prog:Callee[System.__Canon]():System.Type
       nop      
G_M18196_IG03:
       add      rsp, 40
       ret      
; Total bytes of code: 23


; Method Prog:Callee[System.__Canon]():System.Type
G_M53536_IG01:
       sub      rsp, 40
       mov      qword ptr [rsp+20H], rcx
G_M53536_IG02:
       mov      rcx, qword ptr [rcx]
       call     CORINFO_HELP_TYPEHANDLE_TO_RUNTIMETYPE
       nop      
G_M53536_IG03:
       add      rsp, 40
       ret      
; Total bytes of code: 23
```
no nullchecks for generic context, helper calls, etc

The dictionaries are eagerly initialized in NativeAOT and that's why we can skip the null check and delay initialization there. We cannot eagerly initialize dictionaries for CoreCLR. It would be large startup hit and it would break for generic types with infinite instantiation cycles that some popular packages use.

I would focus on CoreCLR with this. I guess that the question-mark commas created by dictionary lookups are hard to deal with. Should we import the dictionary lookups as a new GT note and expand this node to the full dictionary lookup later once the high-level optimizations are done?
